advisories.title: Flood
advisories.forWhom: Anyone in a flood-prone area or caught by rising water
before: Know your nearest high ground and evacuation route.
Keep documents, medicines, and a battery torch in a waterproof bag at waist height.
Store 3 days of drinking water (2 L/person/day) and ready-to-eat food.
Charge phones and power banks; save 112, 108, and 1078 in contacts.
during: Move to higher ground immediately — do not wait for orders.
Never walk or drive through flowing water; 15 cm can knock you down, 30 cm floats a car.
Avoid downed power lines and standing water — electrocution risk.
If trapped, go to the highest floor or roof; signal with bright cloth or light.
after: Do not return until authorities declare the area safe.
Boil or chlorinate all drinking water; flood water contaminates everything.
Discard food that touched flood water — even sealed tins may be unsafe.
Watch for snake bites and skin infections; seek care for any wound.

advisories.title: Cyclone / Severe Storm
advisories.forWhom: Coastal and inland areas in the storm track
before: Secure loose objects (tin sheets, pots, furniture) that can become missiles.
Tape windows in an X or board them; keep curtains drawn.
Fill water containers and bathtubs; power may be out for days.
Identify the strongest interior room (bathroom, hallway) away from windows.
during: Stay indoors, away from windows and glass doors.
If the eye passes — sudden calm — do NOT go out; the back eyewall hits in minutes.
Keep a battery radio on for official updates; do not trust rumours.
If the building fails, shelter under a sturdy table or mattress.
after: Wait for the official all-clear; winds can gust after the centre passes.
Watch for fallen wires, broken glass, and weakened trees.
Check on neighbours, especially elderly and disabled.
Report gas leaks, downed lines, and blocked roads to 112.

advisories.title: Extreme Heat
advisories.forWhom: Everyone, especially elderly, children, pregnant women, outdoor workers, and those with chronic illness
before: Drink water before you feel thirsty — at least 2.5 L/day; carry a bottle.
Schedule hard outdoor work before 10 am or after 5 pm.
Cool your home: curtains drawn, wet towels on windows, fan + bowl of ice.
Check on vulnerable neighbours daily; agree on a check-in time.
during: Stay in the coolest room; wet cloth on neck, wrists, and ankles.
Take cool (not ice-cold) showers; avoid alcohol and heavy meals.
If you feel dizzy, nauseous, cramps, or stop sweating while hot — seek shade, sip water, call 108.
Never leave anyone (or pets) in a parked car — temperatures become lethal in minutes.
after: Keep hydrating for 24 hours after the heat peak.
Watch for delayed heat exhaustion — fatigue, headache, confusion.
Restock water and cooling supplies for the next spell.
advisories.helplines: 112 (emergency), 108 (ambulance), 1075 (national heat helpline), state health dept. local number

advisories.title: Earthquake
advisories.forWhom: Anyone in seismic zones (Himalayan belt, North-East, Kutch, Koyna, etc.)
before: Anchor tall furniture and appliances to walls.
Keep a torch, whistle, and shoes by the bed.
Practice Drop-Cover-Hold On with household members.
Know how to shut off gas and electricity.
during: DROP to hands and knees, COVER head under sturdy table, HOLD ON until shaking stops.
If outdoors, move away from buildings, wires, and slopes.
If driving, pull over away from bridges/overpasses; stay in the vehicle.
after: Expect aftershocks — Drop-Cover-Hold On each time.
Check for gas leaks; if you smell gas, shut off main valve and ventilate.
Text, don't call — lines jam; use 112 for life-threatening only.
Do not enter damaged buildings until inspected.
